english.title: Fail to take reasonable steps to ascertain who is a registrable person or a relevant legal entity, and identify them
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), were

(A)_[a company to which Part 21A of the Companies Act 2006 applied and which]_
(B)_[an officer namely, **(..SPECIFY OFFICER..) of a company to which Part 21A of the Companies Act 2006 applied, namely **(..SPECIFY COMPANY..), and who was in default in that company]_

failed to take reasonable steps to find out if there was anyone who was a registrable person or a registrable relevant legal entity in relation to the company, and, if so, to identify them
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 790D(1) and 790F of the Companies Act 2006.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Civil financial penalties may be issued by the registrar for this offence being a ‘relevant offence’ as defined by section 1132A of the Companies Act 2006. No criminal proceedings may be commenced against a person in respect of conduct amounting to an offence if the person has already been given a financial penalty by the registrar. Further, no financial penalty may be imposed on a person in relation to conduct amounting to an offence if proceedings in respect of that offence are ongoing or the person has been convicted.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
NoneNote
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
